[[File:酒列磯前神社 一の鳥居.JPG|thumb|200px|First torii. The plaque calligraphy is by Prince Akihito Komatsu.]]
'''Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine''' (さかつらいそさきじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki. It is a Meishin-taisha listed in the Engishiki, formerly ranked kokuhei chusha, and currently a Beppyo shrine of Jinja Honcho.

=== Overview ===
The shrine stands on a coastal cape facing the Pacific Ocean. It is closely connected with {{ill|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|es|Santuario Ōarai Isosaki|ja|大洗磯前神社|simple|Ōarai Isosaki Shrine|zh|大洗矶前神社|qid=Q11437230}} across the Naka River, and the two are often regarded as forming a paired cult.

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Main deity
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}
; Co-enshrined
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Onamochi-no-Mikoto}}

The two-deity pairing is common because both appear together in kuni-zukuri myths. At this shrine, Sukunahikona is also associated with Ebisu and Onamochi with Daikokuten.

=== History ===
According to the ''Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku'' (856), divine signs appeared at Oarai Isosaki, with miraculous stones and an oracle declaring the returning deities Onamochi and Sukunahikona. Tradition says Onamochi was enshrined at Oarai and Sukunahikona at Sakatsura, establishing both shrines.

The shrine name is linked to a local "reverse-tilting" rock formation (saka-tsura). Later, it came to be written with the character for sake (酒).

In the Engishiki, it appears as "Sakare Isosaki Yakushi Bosatsu Shrine" in Naka District, Hitachi Province, and is listed as Meishin-taisha. It declined in the medieval period and lost its buildings; in the early modern period it was restored under Mito domain patronage by Tokugawa Mitsukuni and Tokugawa Tsunaeda, with relocation to the current site.

In 1885 it was ranked kokuhei chusha. The official modern name is Sakatsura Isosaki Shrine.

=== Divine rank ===
* 857-08-07: entered official shrine register
* 857-10-15: granted title "Yakushi Bosatsu Meishin"

=== Precinct ===
Notable features include:
* Carving of squirrels and grapes above the haiden front (traditionally attributed to Jingoro Hidari)
* Komainu at the second torii by Showa-era stonemason Iizuka Hyokichi
* Broadleaf tree-lined approach (camellia, tabunoki, sudajii), designated natural monument of Ibaraki Prefecture

* Inari Shrine
* Tenmangu
* Kotohira Shrine
* Fuji Shrine
* Suijin Shrine

=== Site information ===
* Address: Isozaki-cho 4607-2, Hitachinaka, Ibaraki
* Access: Hitachinaka Seaside Railway Minato Line, Ajigaura Station, about 15 minutes on foot
